interest: the standardization system itself — one hull per role, one gun, one torpedo, one engine cartridge
block construction and the hydroformed panel line

the provision habit that wires a hull for equipment nobody has yet — the radar masts, the plot compartments, the bow catapult foundations, the cannon galleries, the 7.7 t aviation cranes. Architecture under §8's premise clause, not a performance claim

the dual-purpose director family. ⚠ NO NAVY HAD A DUAL-PURPOSE MECHANICAL FIRE-CONTROL COMPUTER IN SERVICE IN 1930. HACS I went to sea in Valiant in January 1930 and was anti-aircraft only; the first true DP director anywhere was the American Mark 33 of 1934. [jp30dir] is +5, the interest ceiling, and the director is the MECHANISM of the one-gun interest line and belongs in the same band as the turret it lays
supporting: the fleet direction center — +1 to +2 on the Royal Navy's fighter direction of 1940–41 and ahead of the American CIC of 1942–43
the aero search radar the center was built around. ⚠ Its ship range is 30 km, because ASV Mark I entered service in early 1940 and saw a 1,000-ton ship at about 16 km
par: ship radar. ⚠ Its surface range is 26 km, because nothing in the world saw a ship at 45 km — Type 271 managed about 25 km in 1941 and SG about 28 km in 1942. Its air figure of 130 km on FORMATIONS is verified par: Lexington's CXAM-1 detected the incoming strike at 109 km at Coral Sea

sonar. ⚠ The 1943 scanning set reaches 4,000 m, against a real Type 144 of the same year at about 2,500 m. Scanning at 1943 is +1 on the American QLA of July 1944; depth-finding is exactly par with the British Type 147 of 1943; the ahead-throwing output is a year BEHIND Hedgehog

the 25 mm cannon and its round. ⚠ Its rate is 240 rpm/barrel at 920 m/s. The real Type 96 of 1936 did 220 rpm cyclic on a 15-round box magazine — but the comparator that governs is the world's best of 1929, and that is the belt-fed 2-pdr pom-pom of 1915 at 200 rpm. 250 rpm at 25 mm interpolates between the pom-pom at 40 mm and the Oerlikon S of 1927 at 20 mm and 280 rpm, so it is par with the world and not with Japan. ⚠ THE 240-ROUND INTEGRAL BELT IS NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM AND STAYS: the pom-pom was belt-fed in 1915, and removing the Type 96's 15-round box is a FEED ARCHITECTURE choice under §8's premise clause. It is also the most important thing in the line, because that magazine was the real weapon's dominant tactical defect

shells, bombs, mines, depth charges and rockets. ⚠ THE 1925 SHELL'S PROXIMITY-READY CAVITY IS ARCHITECTURE, NOT A FUZE: the fuze arrives in [jp42shl], and the real VT fuze went into combat on 5 January 1943 aboard Helena, so the fuze itself is +1 at worst

the turbojet, which is at the world's best rather than ahead of it. ⚠ 2,450 kgf at 800 kg in 1944 against the Rolls-Royce Nene, first run 27 October 1944 at 2,268 kgf and 730 kg, and the de Havilland Ghost at 2,404 kgf and 968 kg

both aero engines. ⚠ [jp33aeg] is 790 hp from 27 L at 430 kg in 1933 — 1.84 hp/kg and 29.3 hp/L, just behind a Bristol Mercury VIII at 1.87 and 33.7; [jp39aeg] is 1,090 hp from 27 L at 485 kg in 1939 — 2.25 hp/kg and 40.4 hp/L, just behind a Bristol Taurus II at 2.27 and 41.9. ⚠ BOTH ENGINES ARE AS LIGHT AS PAR ALLOWS AND NO LIGHTER: another 10 kg on either takes it past the best real article of its own layout. Specific output is BEHIND an R-1830 and a Taurus on both engines.
⚠ THE 0.26 kg/hp·h CRUISE FIGURE THAT GIVES THIS NAVY ITS RANGE IS A DOCTRINE CREDIT — the cruising bank, the engine cartridges and a lean-cruise syllabus — NEVER AN ENGINE ONE.

⚠ THE STRIKE TWIN'S SPEED, AND NOTHING ELSE IN THIS NAVY. Flush riveting, aeroformed skins off the hydroformed panel line and gap sealing specified on the drawing are PROCESS and band in Interest; the speed they produce bands here. The twin at 577 km/h in 1939 is about +2 against a Bf 110C at 560, a Whirlwind at 580 in 1940 and a Mosquito at 612 in 1941, and is not to be filed back into par. ⚠ THE FIGHTER IS PAR AND THEN SOME: 565 km/h is BELOW a Spitfire I of 1938 at 582.

the torpedo [jp33tor], which sits BELOW the real Type 93 on both settings — 49 kt to 14,000 m and 32 kt to 32,500 m against the real fish's 48 kt to 20,000 m and 36 kt to 40,000 m. This navy built one torpedo and no other, and it is the one line where the standardization system bought less than the historical article.
cold: the battle line — ten hulls never modernized because the plan refused to spend on them
heavy-caliber naval gunnery entire, which stopped developing in 1922
land-based naval aviation, which the plan never funded because every deck it wanted was floating

⚠ JAPAN'S COLD BAND HOLDS NO EQUIPMENT LINE AT ALL, AND THAT IS ITS STRONGEST FORM. There is no heavy-gun line in this catalog because there was no heavy-gun program; there is no land-based airframe because there was no land-based program; the battle line's ten hulls carry what they carried in 1922. A cold band expressed as an ABSENCE is a design statement and is not a gap to be filled. ⚠ A validator rule requiring every declared band to hold a line was written and withdrawn for this reason.
the 14 cm dual-purpose turret's ballistics, which are the 1916 gun's inside 1930s architecture: the mounting and its director are the modern half and the shell is not.
calibration.notes: Most of what runs deep here is architecture and process under §8's premise clause, not a performance claim. Performance may not exceed +5 anywhere, and nothing in this file does. The air arm's depth is architecture: both aero engines and the Type 39 pair's speed figures sit at PAR, and the turbojet is at the world's best rather than ahead of it.

common.note: One barbette ring, all hulls. A turret change is a crane evolution at any fleet anchorage.

spec.drive: power-worked semi-automatic; fixed loading hoist and any-angle rammer

common.charging: manifold from the ship's high-pressure cascade bank
common.note: The defining component is the charging manifold, not the tubes: every torpedo is stowed inert and brought to life at loading.
One works produces the barrels, the springs and the belts for every mount in the fleet, afloat and airborne alike, off one drawing.

mounts.feed: continuous from the ship; mount craned off complete at barrel life

spec.feed: belt; magazine capacity is a property of the mount

mounts.note: Mount masses are the MOUNT, less ammunition. A belted round weighs 620 g, so an aircraft twin's 320 rounds add 198 kg to the 182 kg mounting.

spec.gyro_sight: naval twin and every combat aircraft; cannon lead and dive/glide bombing computed off the same gyro
spec.unchanged: barrel, round, rate, mounts, magazines, belts

common.asw_round: sinking-head for ship rails, sonar-aimed fans
common.note: The motor plant is a powder line, not a gun works: expansion costs chemistry, not machine tools.

common.swap_conditions: alongside a tender in sheltered water
common.note: The bay is the commitment and the engine improves inside it. Every hull laid down from 1922 carried the same bay whether its engines existed yet or not. The same block is the state railways' locomotive prime mover and the ports' shore generator.
One engine per aircraft type is doctrine: the Type 32 carries the Hibari for the aircraft's whole life, with no uprating program to fragment the spares pool or the schools.

One combat engine per generation: the Type 39 powers both halves of the Type 39 pair unchanged for their entire run — the fighter takes one, the strike twin two from the same crate. No water injection program, no altitude blocks, no mid-life gamble that splits the inventory. No successor radial was ever studied.
Centrifugal flow was set because every stress and surge behavior is knowable early and the compressor forgives what a war economy will do to tolerances. The jet age adds no new fuel line at all.

spec.fuel: wide-cut kerosene from the fleet distillate stream

common.note: Nothing that trains, because a dish that moves is a dish that breaks at sea. Aircraft and radar are one specification. Coverage rises with the production run, not with a refit queue.

Every hull since 1922 has carried the masts, wiring runs and power margins for a set that did not exist — the longest-armed provision in the fleet. Fitting radar is an anchorage evolution measured in days.
One head, one computer, one school, every gunned hull. The 1941 and 1945 steps change what feeds the computer, never where it sits or who runs it.

spec.solutions: full air and surface from radar data alone
spec.tracks: feed the fleet direction center's plot

spec.enables: lays jp42gun without an optical solution

common.note: Every carrier and cruiser since 1922 has carried an armored plot compartment and the fighter-direction radio net wired into it — a room built for a machine nobody could describe when the bulkheads went up. Controlled-intercept capacity, not radar range, is the number a fleet's air defense is rationed by.

spec.fuses: radar search and beacon bearings on one plot

common.note: The set, the depth-charge battery it aims and its school were designed as one artifact — the ship is the sonar's delivery system, not the reverse. Its tables, not its transducers, are the set's real secret.

common.type: compressed-air track catapult and electric recovery crane
common.note: One drawing, all hulls. The rating was chosen in 1928 for an airplane that did not yet exist.

common.halves: ship transmitter; aircraft receiver and transponder

common.note: The merchant marine is the navy's reserve flight-deck tonnage, dispersed in plain sight. The conversion needs no naval yard, so mobilization does not compete with warship construction for slips.
The kit that taught the fleet that aircraft configuration is a stores question. The float set is the configuration the maximum-weight sortie flies in.

spec.exchange: at sea, calm water, ship's crane

common.note: What makes the strike arm a stores item: a tender, ten crates and a swept anchorage are a strike force without a flight deck, and the recess carries the full ordnance set — the fish included — from water. Float squadrons are administered where the crates are, by the fleet train and the forward anchorages, not by the carriers.

spec.exchange: in sheltered water, any 7.7 t aviation crane — cruiser, tender or carrier
spec.water_operation: takeoff and alighting from water; crane recovery — no catapult, no deck recovery

common.air_drop: as built (reinforced vessel + wooden aero shroud)
common.note: The weight was fixed at what a single-engine aircraft lifts from a deck run, and half the navy was sized around it. The torpedo is the fleet's true main battery; everything else in the catalog exists to deliver it. The warhead is built as three modular 100 kg charges for handling, and the depth charge's burster is one of them.

spec.vessel_drive: second generation, +7% energy, settings held synced
spec.homing_head: passive acoustic option, 28 kt terminal seek
spec.release: drop-hardened (reinforced nose cap, jettisoning tail shroud)

common.note: One shell serves surface, air and shore bombardment across the whole fleet, which means there is no wrong ammunition to load, ever. The proximity cavity was cut into the first drawing, seventeen years before the fuze that fills it existed anywhere on earth.

Worked backward from the torpedo the fleet had already frozen: two bombs had to fill the space, stations and weight of one fish. The fleet's only bomb, so the loadout question is a flight-deck decision, not a design-office one.

spec.geometry: pair-shaped in tandem to the torpedo-form recess

common.air_kit: to the bomb form: nose fairing + tail cone, +8 kg per charge -- 162 kg as dropped
common.note: ONE DRUM SERVES BOTH GENERATIONS: the torpedo warhead was already broken into modular charges for handling, so the drum was sized around one of them and nothing new is filled. A later generation is a fuze setting and a thrower pattern, not a new store. Explosive production is one stream feeding two shapes.
common.burster_source: one of the torpedo warhead's three modular 100 kg charges

common.air_kit: drogue-retarded cylinder case in the bomb form
common.note: Stocks are held unassembled: the mine reserve and the torpedo reserve are one inventory until the day they are assembled, invisible to any registry inspection. Case production is sheet-metal work placed with civilian fabricators, invisible in any naval budget.

forms.fits: any bomb-form centerline or recess station; two ride a torpedo-form recess in tandem, mixed with a 650 bomb at will

common.note: Faired to the same lines as the stores they replace, so the drag books needed no new pages. One form only: the torpedo-form recess takes a tandem pair, or a bomb and a tank one-and-one. Fit is by SHAPE, not by aircraft type, so future airframes inherit the tanks for free.

spec.drag: recess drags alike loaded or empty
